title: Confident, Calibrated, or Complicit: Probing the Trade-offs between Safety Alignment and Ideological Bias in Language Models in Detecting Hate Speech
measurement_description: The paper evaluated the performance of Large Language Models in detecting hate speech, specifically measuring the classification accuracy and fairness disparities for content targeting different demographic groups, including religious groups like Jewish people and Muslims.
findings: The study found significant disparities in hate speech detection performance across different target groups. Models achieved the highest accuracy (94.0%) on content targeting 'jewish_people', while performance on other groups, including 'muslims' (75.3%), was lower. This highlights a critical fairness issue, termed 'Unequal Protection', where some communities receive more effective protection from hate speech detection systems than others.
